newsitem.title: CHINA: China bans establishment of new colour TV makers.
newsitem.headline: China bans establishment of new colour TV makers.

text.p: China has banned the establishment of new colour television makers or the expansion of existing plants because supply outstrips demand, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

Local governments and departments under the State Council, or cabinet, are not allowed to approve new production lines or expansions, Chen Wenjie, a senior State Planning Commission official, was quoted as saying.
He did not say how long the ban would be in effect.
Production capacity is more than sufficient to meet domestic demand as well as exports, Chen said.
China produced 21 million colour television sets in 1996 and sold 18 million, the newspaper said without giving comparative figures.
Domestic colour television makers earned 6.0 billion yuan ($722.9 million) in profits in 1996, it said.
About 93 percent of urban families and 30 percent of rural families own colour televisions, totalling about 140 million sets, the newspaper said.
China plans to boost the figure to 97 sets per 100 families in urban areas and at least 40 sets per 100 families in rural areas by the turn of the century, it said.
In 1996, China had 98 colour television makers, five of which have annual production capacity of more than one million sets.
Supply would continue to outstrip demand in the years ahead.
"Domestic demand for colour TVs will be 25 million a year by 2000," Chen said.
Production capacity of colour televisions would surge to 33 million sets a year by 2000, the newspaper said.
Exports were forecast to grow to eight million sets by the year 2000 compared with five million last year, it said.
The government would encourage exports by offering preferential policies on loans and taxes, the newspaper said.
China would crack down on illegal imports of colour television sets and parts, it said but did not say what punishment violators faced.
